title: Plant mitochondria different from animal
question: are plant ones different??
canonical_question: Are plant mitochondria different from animal mitochondria?
summary: Plant and animal mitochondria share the same central chain.
Plants add alternative electron routes that trade ATP for flexibility.

reuse.rationale: Nothing in the branch or course covers plant-specific electron routes.

sections.heading: Same core, different extras
sections.body_md: Plant and animal mitochondria share the same central design: the four complexes, the mobile carriers, and ATP synthase all work the same way. The differences appear as extra parts that plants add on top of this shared machinery.

sections.heading: Alternative routes for electrons
sections.body_md: Plant mitochondria carry an alternative oxidase, a protein that can pass electrons straight to oxygen while bypassing the last complexes. They also have extra NADH dehydrogenases that feed electrons in without being blocked by the usual inhibitors. These routes let a plant burn off spare electrons and give off heat instead of ATP.

sections.heading: Why plants keep the extras
sections.body_md: A plant cannot move to a better spot when conditions change, so flexible energy handling is useful. The alternative routes help a plant cope with stress and cold, and with the demands of running photosynthesis alongside respiration.

key_points: Plant and animal mitochondria share the same central chain.
Plants add an alternative oxidase and extra NADH dehydrogenases.
These extra routes trade ATP for flexibility and heat.
core.bridge_to_parent: It contrasts the animal hand-off just described with the extra routes plants add.
core.bridge_to_objective: It shows that the job of making ATP can be tuned differently across organisms, extending the objective account of energy production.

path.title: Introduction to energy production in the mitochondria
path.summary: Cellular respiration converts nutrients into ATP. Most ATP is made in the mitochondrion.

path.title: Proteins essential for ATP synthesis
path.summary: ATP synthase has a proton-driven rotor and a catalytic head. Complexes I to IV build the proton gradient that drives it.

path.title: Cytochrome c: structure and role
path.summary: Cytochrome c is a small mobile electron carrier. It shuttles electrons from Complex III to Complex IV.

path.title: Electron donation to Complex IV
path.summary: Cytochrome c docks on Complex IV and releases its electron. The electron moves through copper and heme sites to oxygen.
